The `images` regex `[0-9]*\` - the `\` at the end is likely an escaped space. So the regex is `[0-9]* ` which matches zero or more digits followed by a space. This CAN match an empty string (zero digits followed by a space)!

Wait, but the `\` in the magic file format is an escape. Let me check what `\ ` means in the magic file format. In the magic file format, `\ ` is an escaped space. So the regex is `[0-9]* ` which matches zero or more digits followed by a space.

But wait, the regex `[0-9]* ` requires a space after the digits. So it matches zero or more digits followed by a space. If the input starts with a space, this regex matches the space (zero digits followed by a space). The match is ` ` (just the space), which is not empty.

Hmm, but the glibc bug is about regexec not initializing pmatch when the match is zero-length. The regex `[0-9]* ` matches at least one character (the space), so the match is not zero-length.

Let me think about this differently. The glibc bug is about regexec returning 0 but not initializing pmatch. This happens when the regex matches an empty string. A regex like `^` matches an empty string at the start of any line. A regex like `$` matches an empty string at the end of any line.
